# Uploads and transfers

Find image, file, drop-zone and image-group UI in Media & uploads. Choose the interaction surface first; the host owns networking and business outcomes.

## Choose a component

| Scenario | Component | Guidance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Avatar, cover, single verification material | [FileUpload](/en/components/file-upload) | One file through picker or drop, with optional image preview |
| Application or native picker | [ImageUploadSlot](/en/components/image-upload-slot) | State and choose intent, without handling file bytes |
| Multiple files and fixed drop zone | [MediaUpload](/en/components/media-upload) | files layout with independent recovery |
| Nine-image moments | MediaUpload | images layout, maxCount=9, trailing add tile hidden at capacity, host-owned ordering |
| Chat ImageGroup attachments | MediaUpload | images layout with the host's conversation limit |
| Chat transfers and downloads | [TransferProgress](/en/components/transfer-progress), [TransferQueue](/en/components/transfer-queue) | Keep transfer direction explicit |

## Interactive preview

## Drop zone and keyboard

Web supports choosing or dropping files into a bounded region. File hover highlights the zone; leave and drop reset it. Text and links are not treated as files. Mobile and keyboard users retain a native picker. FileUpload hostPicker mode ignores DOM bytes to preserve the host selection boundary.

## Policy and batch errors

accept is a picker hint, not validation. maxCount disables adding when full, but a batch is never silently truncated. Hosts validate the full batch, type, size and duplicates, then expose items/error. Failures retain existing items. FileUpload stays single-file; use MediaUpload for batches.

## Compact image grid

The images layout shows thumbnails without per-image filenames or idle status; accessible labels retain filenames. A corner close icon removes idle images, and cancels active uploads only when the host supports it. Progress and retry stay inside each thumbnail. Provide previewLabel and handle preview with the shared ImagePreview, reusing host-provided URLs without an additional upload. The files layout retains full file information.

## Progress and recovery

Use stable item IDs. selected can offer manual upload; uploading shows determinate or indeterminate progress, with cancellation only when the host can abort; failed retains the file with retry; uploaded offers preview and removal. These controls emit intents only. Hosts fence late results, update items, and create/revoke object URLs. The component never starts networking.

## Integrating existing Web pages

MomentComposer starts at three text rows and grows to eight before scrolling locally. Locations edit in place; visibility uses an adaptive audience surface. Host-provided submission errors stay with the draft, and retry reports the same submit intent. The image picker is the last grid tile, hidden at capacity; there is no separate picker toolbar. Avatar uses FileUpload for preview, upload and retained-file retry. Moments composes MediaUpload through the MomentComposer images slot, preserving image order and removal of queued selections. ImageGroup uses showPicker=false to review the selection; existing message transfer UI owns subsequent progress and retry. item.disabled locks an individual in-flight item. Commands without progress or abort APIs use indeterminate progress without inventing percentages or successful cancellation. Cover settings remain session-local, not remote uploads. Verification materials retain FileUpload hostPicker and controlled material actions.

## Business composition

Verification pages decide which materials are required. Moments and ImageGroup editors reuse the same image grid and submit only host-confirmed material. This iteration provides shared UI without changing identity verification, posting, messaging, or transfer services.

## Platforms and acceptance

MediaUpload is currently experimental Web UI using browser File[] and DOM drops. Its native batch API is not implemented; native hosts retain existing upload/transfer components. Check desktop, 320px, both themes, long names, full nine-image grids, cancellation, disabled states and recovery. Demos only simulate local state and never upload to a server.
